result.report:
PASS for Theorem A, Theorem B on the stated curves and their ordinary open subspaces, Corollary C, and the separately asserted finite-separable reverse implication. This does not close the original finite-Galois gate or P06.2 recognition.

The finite-algebra argument is valid without reducedness or division by two in K. Bounded coordinate maps identify the completed tensor product with a finite complete direct sum. The linear kernel calculation establishes B^σ=A, including in characteristic two. Factoring the separable quadratic polynomial over H(x), uniqueness of finite-extension absolute values, and the invariant-idempotent argument establish the actual singleton/two-point fibre alternatives and their orbits. Compact inverse images and the compact-complement shrinking argument are justified in Hausdorff carriers. The minimal-prime argument establishes upstairs curve purity; equality of global dimensions alone is not substituted for it. Goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness persist.

The same-carrier comparison under finite restriction of the ground field is justified by common analytic sections, moment charts and coefficient-nullity relations. It establishes the ordinary form comparison used for σ, without asserting descent through π.

Under (H), all three coefficient pairs have norm-one entries and pairwise norm-one determinants. Consequently any two traces cannot both fall below the maximum magnitude. Equation (4) holds throughout the neighbourhood: unequal magnitudes prevent cancellation, while equal magnitudes force at least one chosen trace to attain the maximum. Applying this to f_i and f_if_j gives every δ_iδ_j. Pairing the factors of each even-total-degree δ-monomial proves invariant polynomial descent. The required trace units are secured by finite shrinking. All halves used here are real coefficients.

Both local approximation cases are established. At singleton fibres, the coefficient average is invariant and Gaussian convolution followed by polynomial truncation supplies C² convergence on one fixed invariant box. At two-point fibres, the explicitly conjugate, disjoint pieces glue to invariant analytic units, which belong to A; this proves the claimed exact local scalar descent. No topological covering assertion is needed.

For compact tests, the finite partition produces a fixed compact D. Products extend smoothly by zero because each cutoff support is compactly contained in its ordinary open. Equation (9) holds globally, and pullback supports are compact. Combining the fixed cutoff moments with the fixed error moments bounds all differentiated coefficients through the product rule. Domain restriction preserves the relevant calibrated top measures. On each one-cell, |ΣH_kl v_kv_l|≤rMεΣv_k²; finite positive cell calibrations therefore give the asserted total-variation convergence. Constant or lower-dimensional moment images contribute zero top measure. Actual generic multiplicities remain in the calibration. Boundedness of h on the fixed compact support then establishes (11).

The averaging calculation preserves the field normalizations: the factor two for same-carrier ground-field restriction cancels in the σ-isomorphism identity, whereas scalar base-change pushforward has no factor two. Finite saturation preserves compactness. Equation (13), followed by the proved differentiated approximation, controls every upstairs scalar test and proves ascent. Pulling back downstairs compact tests proves descent. For arbitrary finite separable extensions, the finite tensor decomposition and minimal-prime proof extend directly, establishing the additional reverse implication only. Finite quadratic towers follow by induction with every stage's (H) established as a hypothesis.

The Q₂ example and the residue-degree-two Newton argument are valid. Independent exact computations confirmed polarization, all three determinant identities, and all 110 even-delta monomials in two moments through total degree six. These computations supplement the analytic proof; they do not verify a current equation or artifact hashes.

Harmless source clarifications are necessary. The local criterion in CLD 15.1.2 requires a smooth Euclidean coefficient; this follows from 15.1.1(b), the definitions, and the closed-image extension argument. In 13.2.8, the filtration identifies ℓ as the generic length of the coherent module F, with F=O_X for structural multiplicities. The cutoff citation is certified only in the compact-F, finite-cover specialization explicitly used by the manuscript. The broader fixed-index compact-support wording for arbitrary countable-at-infinity F cannot be used: a one-set cover of a noncompact F would require a compactly supported function equal to one everywhere. This citation-scope clarification does not change any declared theorem or its compact-support construction. GJR's cited result concerns weakly smooth forms; CLD 16.3.3 gives G-tropical regularity; Conrad–Temkin concerns analytic morphism properties. None supplies an ordinary-form descent premise here.

Every essential external input below was checked against the cited primary version and its proof or construction where provided. No prior verdict, author-audit label, recognition theorem, inseparable note, infinite-extension argument, or two-sign regularization claim is used.

passages.statement: For a complete non-Archimedean field k, a k-affinoid algebra A is noetherian with closed ideals, M(A) is compact Hausdorff, and M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective. Every point of M(A) has rational affinoid neighbourhoods inside prescribed ordinary open neighbourhoods, with defining inequalities strict at the point. Good analytic spaces have an affinoid neighbourhood basis, and ordinary opens are analytic domains. Affinoid fibre products use completed tensor products; complete scalar projection is surjective and inverse images of analytic domains carry their base-change structures. Finite Banach algebras with their finite-module topology are affinoid, and finite analytic morphisms are boundaryless. Strict affinoid dimension is Krull dimension; scalar extension preserves affinoid analytic dimension; analytic domains preserve local dimension. (CLD v2 §§11.1.2, 11.1.5–9, 11.2.3, 11.4.4.)

On a topologically separated analytic space, ordinary smooth forms admit ordinary open moment-chart presentations by analytic units and smooth coefficient forms on paralinéaire subsets. A smooth coefficient form on P∩U extends to the ambient Euclidean open U when P∩U is closed in U. For a compact G-tropical space with chart f and a coefficient form α on a paralinéaire set containing f(X), its pullback vanishes exactly when α restricts to zero on f(X); on arbitrary G-tropical spaces, vanishing is equivalent to coefficient nullity on every compact domain image. Smooth pullback preserves products and commutes with d′ and d″. (CLD v2 1.9.4, 3.3.12, 3.4.1–4, 6.2.1–2, 15.1.1–2.)

For a good topologically separated analytic space X, a compact subset F, and a finite ordinary open cover (U_i) of F, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth functions θ_i on X, each with compact support contained in U_i, whose sum equals one near F. No global paracompactness of X is required. (Compact specialization of CLD v2 15.2.2, 15.2.9 and its supporting cutoff construction.)

A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has its canonical calibrated tropical structure, compatible with analytic-domain restriction, and a continuous real multiplier h defines the integration current by ω↦∫hω_Rad on compact smooth top forms. Smooth top forms are locally integrable, and compact smooth top forms are integrable. On a compact curve affinoid, a moment has compact polyhedral image and a pleasant top-dimensional skeleton admitting a finite cell refinement with positive standard canonical calibration; top-form integration is coefficient contraction against that calibration followed by cell integration. (CLD v2 §§5.4, 5.8, 5.10, 7.3.5, 14.1–3, 15.7.1–2.)

For an analytic morphism f:Y→X, a complete valued extension L/k, x_L above x=f(y), and the scalar-extended morphism f_L, deg_y(f)=Σ_z deg_z(f_L), where z ranges over points above y in f_L⁻¹(x_L). For a finite fibre, its total degree is the H(x)-dimension of its actual fibre algebra. For a coherent module F and an upstairs irreducible component lying over a downstairs component, its scalar-extended generic length is ℓ_L=μℓ, where ℓ is the downstairs generic length of F and μ is the upstairs generic multiplicity of the scalar extension of X_red. (CLD v2 13.2.8, 13.3.1–3.)

Let X be a topologically separated k-analytic space of level n, L/k a complete extension, and π:X_L→X scalar projection. For a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ and its scalar-extended skeletal subset Σ_L with calibration μ_L, π_*μ_L=μ. For an (n,n)-G-form ω with tropically Borel coefficients, π_*(ω_L,Bor)=ω_Bor; if ω is locally integrable, π_*(ω_L,Rad)=ω_Rad. (CLD v2 14.3.6, 15.3.1.)

Let X be a topologically separated k-analytic space of level n, L/k a complete extension, and π:X_L→X scalar projection. For a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ and its scalar-extended skeletal subset Σ_L with calibration μ_L, π_*μ_L=μ. For an (n,n)-G-form ω with tropically Borel coefficients, π_*(ω_L,Bor)=ω_Bor; if ω is locally integrable, π_*(ω_L,Rad)=ω_Rad. (CLD v2 14.3.6, 15.3.1.)

For a finite complete extension F/k and an F-analytic space Z of level n, its same carrier with restricted k-analytic structure Z₀ has the same dimension and skeletal subsets. On each such skeletal subset, the canonical calibrations satisfy μ_Z₀=[F:k]μ_Z. (CLD v2 14.4.3.)

Let f:Y→X be a morphism between k-analytic spaces of level n that is finite above the complement of a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n. For p∈{n−1,n} and a locally integrable (p,n)-G-form ω, f*ω is locally integrable and f_*((f*ω)_Rad)=dc(f)ω_Rad, with the actual calibrated degree dc(f). (CLD v2 15.4.1–3.)
For a morphism X→Y of k-analytic spaces and any analytic extension L/k, ∂(X_L/Y_L)⊆π⁻¹(∂(X/Y)); in particular ∂X_L⊆π⁻¹(∂X). (Gubler–Rabinoff, arXiv:2506.13548v2, §2.11(5′).)
